preconditions.description: Input consists of two integers n (number of pairs) and k (number of colors), each between 2 and 200000 inclusive.

postconditions.description: If no valid coloring exists, output is exactly 'NO'. Otherwise, output starts with 'YES' followed by exactly 2n integers representing valid b_i and g_i pairs.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(b) <= k and 1 <= int(g) <= k for b, g in zip(b_i, g_i)) if 'YES' in stdout else True
postconditions.description: For every pair (b_i, g_i), both colors are integers between 1 and k inclusive.

postconditions.expression: len(set(zip(b_i, g_i))) == n if 'YES' in stdout else True
postconditions.description: No two pairs (b_i, g_i) and (b_j, g_j) are identical for i ≠ j.

postconditions.expression: all(b != g for b, g in zip(b_i, g_i)) if 'YES' in stdout else True
postconditions.description: For every pair, the man's costume color b_i is not equal to the woman's costume color g_i.

postconditions.expression: all(b_i != b_j and g_i != g_j for i, j in zip(range(n-1), range(1, n))) if 'YES' in stdout else True
postconditions.description: For every two consecutive pairs, the man's costume colors and woman's costume colors differ.
